notes: `createAuth` keeps the application's configuration: the admin, organization, two-factor, generic OIDC, and Stripe plugins, argon2 password hashing, invitations and the self-signup policy, translated email copy, workspace hand-over on account deletion, and its account management helpers.

The secret stays the one each deployment generated on first start and keeps in the `authSecret` deployment setting, passed to `createAuth`, instead of `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`: replacing it would sign everyone out and make stored OAuth tokens unreadable.
`baseURL` is `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, the name deployments already set; without it, `handler` moves each request to its public origin so OAuth redirect URIs stay public behind a proxy.
Sign-in allows 10 attempts a minute and sign-up 5, tighter than the recipe, and sessions last 30 days, refreshed daily.
`useSecureCookies` is off because `src/server/authCookies.ts` marks cookies secure per request, since self-hosted installs serve both HTTP and HTTPS.

`tanstackStartCookies()` is not used: server functions whose `auth.api` call sets cookies, such as impersonation, ask for `returnHeaders` and copy them through `src/server/authCookies.ts`, which also decides the `Secure` flag per request.

Social providers come from `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID` and `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_SECRET`, optionally `AUTH_<PROVIDER>_ENABLED`, or from the super admin settings, and include OIDC, in `src/adapters/auth.ts`.
`src/db/schema/auth.ts` holds the auth tables with the organization, admin, two-factor, and Stripe columns, in SQLite and, in `src/db/schema-postgres/auth.ts`, PostgreSQL.
`src/core/authFailures.ts` holds the failure classifiers in the domain layer, because `src/core/auth.ts` builds the translated sign-in messages from them.

`src/server/session.ts` and `src/server/random.ts` are left out: the composition root's `identity`, `requireIdentity`, and `workspace` own session lookups, and invite tokens use `node:crypto` directly.
`localRedirectPath` is left out because sign-in has no `next` destination.
`better-auth` and `@better-auth/stripe` are pinned to the same version and grouped in Dependabot because the Stripe plugin pins the core version.

`ci.yml` is left out: `.github/workflows/docker.yml` runs `pnpm check:ci` with a PostgreSQL service so both database targets are tested, splits the unit tests and end-to-end suites into shards, scans the image, and releases, so one workflow carries checks, release, and deploy.
Dependabot ignores `@better-auth/stripe`, which must move with `better-auth`.
Dependabot groups `better-auth` with `@better-auth/*`, because Better Auth's plugins pin its core version and a lone bump splits the types.

SQLite is the default target and PostgreSQL the other, chosen by `DATABASE_URL` in `src/db/config.ts`; `database-postgres` is not adopted because its own RECIPE.md leaves a dual target to the application, and the PostgreSQL side (`src/db/backends/postgres.ts`, `src/db/postgresConnection.ts`, `src/db/schema-postgres/`, `drizzle-postgres/`, `drizzle.postgres.config.ts`) is application code that follows the same decisions: ten lazy connections, numeric parsers, dropped notices, and migrations from the working directory.

`src/db/database.ts` and its tests are left out: both targets sit behind `DatabaseBackend` in `src/db/backends/`, and SQLite is wrapped in a serialized async facade (`src/db/connection.ts`) so repository code is the same on both. `SQLiteBackend` sets the same pragmas, writes `backups/stlquest-pre-migration-<time>.sqlite` before pending migrations, migrates with foreign keys off, runs `PRAGMA foreign_key_check`, and runs `quick_check` at start; review each change to `src/db/database.ts` against it.
The database file stays `$DATA_DIR/stlquest.sqlite`, the migrations stay in `drizzle/` with their history, and `drizzle.config.ts` reads the schema from `src/db/schema/index.ts`.
`scripts/database.ts` is left out: `scripts/backup.ts` (`pnpm backup`) writes a checked `VACUUM INTO` copy and the integration key beside it, and restores are documented operator steps.
Migrations are read from the working directory for both dialects, and the image copies `drizzle/` and `drizzle-postgres/` to `/app`; `.oxfmtrc.json` ignores both `meta/` directories.
`DATA_DIR` defaults to `/data` everywhere, and development uses `data-dev/` through `just dev`.
`better-sqlite3` stays on 13, the major the application already ran.

`scripts/databaseFile.ts` is left out: `src/db/paths.ts` already names `stlquest.sqlite` once for both the application and `scripts/backup.ts`, and every recipe file that reads `databaseFileName` is left out.

`deploy.yml` is left out: `.github/workflows/docker.yml` builds one multi-architecture release candidate on `main`, runs the end-to-end suites against it, releases with Changesets, publishes `latest`, `vX.Y.Z`, and `sha-<commit>` for self-hosters, and deploys that digest to Dokploy with `deploy-dokploy-image`.

The image is also the self-hosted product: it keeps OCI labels, the licences, `/prints` with `PRINTS_DIR`, and a health check every 30 seconds on `${PORT}`, so Unraid and TrueNAS installs that change the port stay healthy.
The build stage copies only the sources, catalogs, migrations, and scripts the build reads instead of `COPY . .`, so documentation changes keep the install and build layers cached.

`src/server/shutdown.ts` reads the `AppState` that `app.ts` keeps under `Symbol.for('stlquest.app')` and closes its instance once the start promise settles, because the composition root is asynchronous; it replaces the signal handlers that exited before requests in flight finished, and logs a failure through pino.
Previews keep their `pr-<number>.stl.quest` host behind the shared preview basic auth, a seeded account, and `scripts/previewDeploy.ts` as the deploy script, which sets their environment.
`vite.config.ts` keeps the `X-Robots-Tag` route rule for `/api/**` on the Nitro plugin.
`authEmails` and `PRODUCT_NAME` are left out: `src/server/auth.ts` writes the reset and verification emails in the account's language around `send`.

`emailDelivery` is left out: `resolveSmtpConfig` uses `SMTP_HOST` and its companions only when `SMTP_HOST` is set and otherwise the mail server saved in the super admin settings, and `buildEmailDelivery` turns either into a delivery.
`workspaceEmailDelivery` sends through a workspace's own mail server; on the hosted service it resolves the host for every exchange, refuses private addresses, and passes the name as `servername`.
`brandedEmailParts` attaches a workspace logo as a `cid` image and sets the workspace's display name and reply-to address.
`src/adapters/workspaceEmailDelivery.test.ts` covers the hosted workspace path against a mocked transport.
`SMTP_SECURE` accepts `1`, `yes`, and `on` as well as `true`, through the application's `environmentFlag`, because existing self-hosted deployments set it that way.
`PostHogIdentity` takes `properties`, which the root route fills with the member's role and whether they are a super admin, read when identifying so a role change alone does not identify again.
`PostHogIdentity` renders in the root route's content inside `PostHogIntegration`, and does nothing while the deployment has telemetry off, because PostHog is then never loaded.

`rpc` does not look up the session to pass `authenticatedDistinctId` to `observeServerFunction`, which would add a session query to every server function: server function spans carry the browser session, and their logs and exceptions carry the verified person through the request log context that `requireIdentity` and `workspace` set.

`src/server/optionalTelemetry.ts` wraps `createTelemetry` in `OptionalPostHogTelemetry`, which honours the deployment's telemetry setting: with telemetry off at startup it creates the client without a token, so nothing is sent and exception autocapture installs no handlers, and every capture checks the setting again.
The composition root creates the telemetry inside its own asynchronous `createApp` after reading that setting, and closes it after the workspaces, notifications, and realtime publisher.
Server functions are observed through `observeRpc`, which runs `observeServerFunction` only while an application instance owns telemetry, so `rpc` works before `app()` starts and in tests.

`reportServerFunctionFailure` is removed: `rpc` logs failures through the pino logger, whose hooks already send every error-level record with an `err` to PostHog as an exception and every record as a log, so the recipe's reporter would report each failure twice.

Pino records reach `telemetry.log` with their attributes, which already carry the request id, session, person, and workspace from the request context; Pino's trace and fatal levels map to debug and error.
`serviceName` is `stlquest`, so browser logs and metrics report as `stlquest-web`, with the release as `serviceVersion`.

PostHog starts while the first enabled `PostHogIntegration` renders instead of when `src/client/posthog.tsx` loads, and `PostHogIntegration` takes `enabled`, because each deployment can turn telemetry off in its settings and the published image carries the project token; it still starts before any child's effect runs.
`PostHogIntegration` takes the translated `fallback` the root route renders.

`postHogOptions` in `src/client/posthogOptions.ts` adds the application's `before_send` filters (expected storage rejections, duplicate server function exceptions, opaque cross-origin script errors), turns off console error capture, masks all text and element attributes, and blocks `.ph-no-capture` in replay, because workspaces hold names, filenames, and notes.

The Docker build maps the existing repository variables `POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID` and `POSTHOG_HOST` and secret `POSTHOG_API_KEY` onto the `POSTHOG_CLI_*` names in `.github/workflows/docker.yml`, which is this application's deploy workflow, and keeps the `GITHUB_*` build arguments that name the uploaded release.
`vitest.config.ts` defines `__APP_VERSION__`, which `postHogOptions` reads.

Channels are the application's `channelPolicy` in `src/server/realtimeChannels.ts`, tested in `src/server/realtimeChannels.test.ts`: each connection token grants the server-side `workspace:<id>` channel of the workspace the session is in, and `board:<slug>` presence takes a subscription token only for members who see the whole board; `centrifugo.json` defines those two namespaces.
`RealtimeViewer` carries the viewer's `workspace`, and the composition root looks it up through `workspace(headers)`, so a signed-out caller or a missing workspace answers 401.

The secret keeps the deployed names: `STLQUEST_REALTIME_SECRET`, generated into `$DATA_DIR/realtime-secret` or the file `STLQUEST_REALTIME_SECRET_FILE` names, with `stlquest-development-realtime-secret` outside production; `STLQUEST_REALTIME_API_KEY` and `STLQUEST_REALTIME_API_URL` set a separate Centrifugo key and address, which the fast end-to-end server uses, and tests publish nowhere.

The supervisor seeds a preview before starting when `STLQUEST_SEED_PREVIEW=true`, and with `STLQUEST_DISTRIBUTED=true` gives Centrifugo the Redis engine at `REDIS_URL`, so replicas share publications and presence.

Centrifugo accepts any origin unless `APP_URL` is set, which self-hosted deployments do not set because they are reached by several names; Caddy still refuses a WebSocket whose `Origin` names another host.
The event bus in `src/adapters/events.ts` publishes each workspace event as `{ event }` on its workspace channel through `app().realtime.publish`, and storage changes to the other replicas.
The token route keeps its path at `src/routes/api/realtime/token.ts` and runs inside the request context for logs.

`src/client/workspaceUpdates.ts` refreshes every active query on a workspace publication or an unrecovered reconnect and leaves a deleted workspace; the root route keys `RealtimeProvider` by the workspace.
`just dev` starts `pnpm realtime` in the background and removes its container when Vite exits.

`src/server/app.ts` keeps the application's asynchronous composition root: `app()` returns a promise, because opening the repository, distributed coordination, and storage recovery are asynchronous, and the instance reconciles workflow changes and closes its resources in its own order. It lives on `globalThis` under `Symbol.for('stlquest.app')`.

`src/server/origins.ts` reads `BETTER_AUTH_URL` and `BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` instead of `APP_URL`, the names self-hosted deployments already set, and always accepts the forwarded origin instead of requiring `TRUST_PROXY`, because self-hosted installs run behind whatever proxy the operator chose and rejecting it would break every mutation there.
`isSameOriginRequest` takes `allowReferer`, which the tus `HEAD` check uses because browsers send no `Origin` on it.
`src/server/middleware.ts` drops `canonicalHost`: a self-hosted install is reached by LAN names and addresses as well as `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, and redirecting those would lock operators out.
The stale server function message is the application's English copy, which the browser matches to show the translated message.
`src/server/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` adds `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` for meshoptimizer, `blob:` workers and images, and the Gravatar, Discord, and Google avatar hosts.
`/api/**` responses keep `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from a Nitro route rule in `vite.config.ts`.
`rpc` and `mutationRpc` run inside the request's locale and log failures through the application's pino logger.

`healthResponse` logs a failed check as a warning through the pino logger, so a restart loop does not report an exception per probe; the health route checks the repository and upload staging inside one `checkDependency` reported as `service_unavailable`.
The Query client keeps `staleTime: 0`, because realtime invalidation refetches every active query, and shows mutation failures as toasts.
Chunk recovery keeps the `stlquest:chunk-reload` storage key and reveals the application's translated `chunk-load-failure` notice in `UpdateNotices`.

The root route keeps the document in `component`, because `<html lang>` follows the session's locale from a suspense query, and keeps its own head tags, theme and translation guard scripts, and providers.
The router keeps the application's `RouteError` and translated not-found page, and leaves scroll restoration off.
`src/styles.css` imports `tw-animate-css` and the application's theme stylesheets after Tailwind.
`vite.config.ts` keeps the development `/api` image workaround, the `__APP_VERSION__` define, and resolves the `@/*` alias with `resolve.tsconfigPaths`.
`AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`, which keeps the application's agent guide and carries the recipe paragraph under **Recipes**.
`tsconfig.json` keeps `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false`, `resolveJsonModule`, and the `@/*` path alias, because the codebase predates the strict preset and indexes arrays throughout.

`.oxlintrc.json` turns off `typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` in tests, because recipe tests assert indexes with `!` and the application's `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false` makes those assertions redundant.
`.oxlintrc.json` also extends the `domain.json` preset, which keeps `src/core` free of IO and framework imports, and turns off the rules the codebase does not follow.
`.oxfmtrc.json` keeps its schema and ignores generated catalogs, deploy templates, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
`vitest.config.ts` resolves the `@` alias, runs files one at a time in forks because tests share the `globalThis` app singleton and SQLite state, and keeps the node environment.

`check` runs `check:ci` and then the tests, and `check:ci` keeps the application's extra gates: Changesets, Markdown links, both Drizzle dialects, the equipment catalogs, Unraid metadata, and the backup CLI.
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` keeps the application's overrides and peer rules, and allows builds for `argon2`, which it installs.
`vitest` stays on 5, the major the application already ran.
`changesets:check` runs `scripts/checkChangesets.mjs`, copied from ras-stack, because the application releases with Changesets.

The server side is the application's own and its recipe files are left out: `src/server/uploads.ts` and `src/adapters/tus.ts` run the tus server per workspace at `/api/upload` (`src/routes/api/upload.$.ts`), stamp the workspace into metadata, store on disk under `$DATA_DIR` or in shared S3 staging in distributed mode, validate model metadata, create or complete a print request when an upload finishes, and keep their limits and storage quotas in `src/server/uploadGuards.ts` and `src/server/storagePolicy.ts`; review each change to the recipe's server files against them.
Upload storage paths and the S3 staging layout are unchanged.
`uploadFile` posts to `/api/upload`, the path the server and in-flight uploads already use.

`uploadFile` takes `fingerprint`, which the upload form scopes to the workspace and request fields so uploads already in flight keep resuming, and `shouldRetry`, which stops retrying a 423 while a storage migration pauses uploads.
`vite.config.ts` prebundles `tus-js-client`, whose CommonJS dependencies the browser cannot load unbundled in development.
